statements.quote: In the future, ethics and compassion will be the most crucial human qualities healers can possess, and our AI buddies can take care of the knowledge base.
statements.context: Opening line (sincere, before the parody begins) of a Dante Canto III parody about GenAI in clinical care. The author predicts a division of labor in future healthcare: human clinicians supply ethics and compassion while AI systems hold the knowledge base.
statements.post_title: Abandon Most Hope, Ye Who Enter Healthcare.
statements.finder_note: General trend forecast, no date. Sincere framing line that precedes the satire.

statements.quote: Thus was the character count reached, and yet I realized I had many iterations yet to go before answers to my patients most crucial queries would be found.
statements.context: Closing line of the parody, narrator's voice (the author as clinician using GenAI in an EHR). After stale, wrong and truncated responses, he concludes that many more iterations of the technology are needed before AI answers patients' most crucial clinical questions. The underlying claim (GenAI is far from answering crucial clinical queries) reads as the author's sincere view.
statements.post_title: Abandon Most Hope, Ye Who Enter Healthcare.
statements.finder_note: Borderline: fictional framing, vague horizon ('many iterations yet to go'). Implies answers eventually come, but not soon.

statements.quote: I humbly submit that if HHS covers brain stimulation treatment more broadly than it does medications, the problem will resolve more quickly.
statements.context: Closing argument of a post on HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s program to reduce antidepressant prescribing (reported by Ellen Barry in the NYT). The author argues antidepressant discontinuation raises suicide risk and that CMS/HHS should remove prior authorization and prior-medication-trial requirements for TMS and other neuromodulation. Conditional forecast: broader HHS coverage of brain stimulation than of medications leads to faster resolution of the overmedication problem.
statements.post_title: Crucial Context for HHS Secretary Kennedy's Anti-Antidepressant Push
statements.finder_note: Conditional ('if HHS covers ... then'). The condition is a policy the author advocates; the outcome ('the problem will resolve more quickly') is loosely defined.

statements.quote: the links at the bottom of the article in The NY Times give us a tantalizing hint at what the future could look like—or what the present looks like, if you are a reader of this newsletter.
statements.context: The author says the NYT article on Kennedy's antidepressant plan omitted brain stimulation, then points to a linked NYT brain stimulation article as a hint of the future of non-drug depression care. He lists ProlivRx, Flow, TMS, DBS, SWIFT, SAINT, One-D, Prism, and companies Salma Health, Radial (his own), Beckley Clinical, Mindful Health Solutions as that present/future.
statements.post_title: Crucial Context for HHS Secretary Kennedy's Anti-Antidepressant Push
statements.finder_note: Hedged, vague implied forecast that brain stimulation is the future of non-pharmacologic depression treatment. Mentions Radial (author's company).

statements.quote: All of these tools are becoming a standard part of Brain Medicine care. This kind of care, when it's deployed as Dr. Carpenter does, will require multiple disciplines working together, and it will enabled by AI.
statements.context: Discussing Dr. Linda Carpenter's iTBS-for-ADHD trial (Brain Stimulation, 2026), which combined TMS with MRI guidance and concurrent EEG. The author says this supports his 'brain medicine is here' thesis (advanced in the newsletter and at Radial): TMS, MRI and EEG tools are becoming standard parts of brain medicine care.
statements.post_title: Finally, ADHD Has A Published accelerated TMS Trial
statements.finder_note: Trend claim (present progressive) that implies future standardization. Mentions Radial (author's company).

statements.quote: This kind of care, when it’s deployed as Dr. Carpenter does, will require multiple disciplines working together, and it will enabled by AI.
statements.context: Same passage on the brain medicine thesis: the author forecasts that multimodal brain medicine care (TMS plus MRI plus EEG, as in Carpenter's lab) will require multidisciplinary teams and will be enabled by AI.
statements.post_title: Finally, ADHD Has A Published accelerated TMS Trial
statements.finder_note: Compound claim: multidisciplinary teams and AI enablement. No date.

statements.quote: That suggests that the difference that Dr. Carpenter has detected is actually a very large one—anything you can see clearly in a small sample is more likely to be a big difference at scale, if it replicates.
statements.context: Interpreting the results of the 34-adolescent double-blind sham-controlled crossover trial of iTBS for ADHD (significant effects on parent-reported working memory, ADHD symptoms, anger, depression, anxiety). The author infers the effect is likely large at scale, conditional on replication.
statements.post_title: Finally, ADHD Has A Published accelerated TMS Trial
statements.finder_note: Conditional expectation about effect size at scale; partly statistical reasoning rather than a dated call.

statements.quote: My personal hunch is the much more refractory nature of the SNT sample is what matters here, but time will tell.
statements.context: Comparing one-year durability of BrainsWay SWIFT accelerated dTMS (interim 64-patient follow-up with high sustained remission) against SNT long-term data that needed personalized re-treatment in many patients. Author expects the durability gap to be explained by the SNT cohort's greater treatment resistance rather than by the protocol.
statements.post_title: I Was On Good Morning America Today
statements.finder_note: Hedged mechanistic call awaiting future evidence. Author was an investigator on the SWIFT trial and coauthor of the durability abstract.

statements.quote: Thanks, friends and coauthors at Brainsway, Magnus, Ampa, and others as we push accelerated TMS (and dTMS) protocols into the mainstream.
statements.context: After the author's Good Morning America segment featuring a patient's recovery with BrainsWay SWIFT accelerated dTMS. Author frames the national attention as part of an effort to move accelerated TMS and dTMS protocols into mainstream clinical practice.
statements.post_title: I Was On Good Morning America Today
statements.finder_note: Weak: describes an ongoing effort with an implied expectation of mainstream adoption. Ampa is one of the author's own organizations.

statements.quote: So there you have it—I may be on to not only one thing, but two for depression.
statements.context: After summarizing the JAMA Psychiatry proof-of-concept RCT of tocilizumab (IL-6 inhibition) in difficult-to-treat depression with low-grade inflammation (n=30; no endpoint significant, remission and response favored tocilizumab, baseline hs-CRP tracked improvement). Author suggests his two long-held bets, accelerated dTMS and the inflammation/autoimmune link to depression, will both be borne out.
statements.post_title: I Was On Good Morning America Today
statements.finder_note: Hedged compound claim: two implied calls (accelerated dTMS; IL-6/inflammation as a depression treatment target) in one sentence.

statements.quote: Will United pay more to the company it will later acquire using its increased revenue to justify the acquisition costs while increasing the cost of care for its services busines s and thus increasing its share of the medical loss ratio on both sides of the ledger? Yes, yes, it will.
statements.context: Satirical 'math behind a scam' essay on private equity in healthcare. Author describes the PE roll-up playbook: buy 51% of a practice, negotiate higher payer contracts, then sell to a payer-owned services arm (United, Cigna, CVS). Rhetorical question answered in the affirmative: United will pay more to companies it later acquires, raising the cost of care and its services-side share of the medical loss ratio.
statements.post_title: Is Private Equity a Bad Deal?
statements.finder_note: Generic pattern claim in a satirical essay; reads sincere. Source text has typo 'busines s'.
